topic: General-r transition-honest counterfactual-entry inference under strong donor factors. For each n observe mutually independent Gaussian blocks X=A+E, R=u+e, C=v+f with known variance, known fixed rank r, singular values of A of order n, fixed incoherence and bounded entries, u in row(A), and v in col(A); the missing untreated mean is theta=u A^+ v and neither target loading is bounded away from zero. Construct an explicit donor-only truncated-SVD interval and prove uniform asymptotic coverage, expected length within a fixed constant of w(P)=sigma sqrt(||uA^+||^2+||A^+v||^2)+sigma^2||A^+||_F, oracle Gaussian length along every sequence where the second-order term is negligible relative to the first, and a matching local KL-neighborhood length lower bound at interior sequences. Compute the interval by fixed-dimensional Gaussian minimum-distance inversion or a certified analytic outer formula plus an observable donor-error allowance and bounded spectral-gate fallback. Credit Yan--Wainwright arXiv:2401.13665 for the panel expansion and Bei--Navjeevan arXiv:2602.07377 for general first-order-degeneracy inference; the narrow new object is the complete general-r strong-donor panel transfer and all-sequence length theorem. Xia--Yan--Wainwright arXiv:2412.09482 and CAST are the same-question consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A fresh derivation obtained the exact conditional Gaussian experiment after donor-only SVD and the sandwich identity V^T X_r^+ U=(MM^T)(U^T X_r V)^(-1)(LL^T), giving an explicit n^(-2)/n^(-3) perturbation bound. A fixed observable allowance was shown to have uniform failure probability at most exp(-n/2)+3(e+n)^(-6) and expected allowance divided by w(P) at most K[log(e+n)/sqrt(n)+log^2(e+n)/n]. The presolve re-derived general-r coverage, transition-order expected length, every-diverging-sequence oracle length, and the two-point/four-corner local lower bound; it also derived an analytic outer interval that avoids nonlinear endpoint optimization. Rank-two calculations checked repeated singular values, cancellation, zero loadings, and spectral failures; current-source checks found no complete-package collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove certified finite-precision implementation theorem C: outward SVD, cutoff, and spectral-gate errors must preserve coverage while their extra expected length is o(w(P)) uniformly. EARLY KILL TEST: Certify the analytic outer interval for the rank-two repeated-singular-value donor with outward error o(1/n) uniformly from zero through B sqrt(n) loading norms and a valid uncertain-gate fallback; stop or change construction if joint zero or arbitrarily slow divergence breaks the budget. open_problems.open_problem: Can a donor-only truncated-SVD interval for theta=uA^+v remain uniformly valid through joint first-order degeneracy while attaining transition-scale expected length, oracle Gaussian length in every first-order-dominant sequence, and a matching local-KL length lower bound for general fixed rank?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Yan--Wainwright's normalized Gaussian approximation excludes joint-zero and arbitrarily slow-loading transitions even though its appendix isolates the surviving bilinear donor-noise term; CAST inherits a projected-loading restriction, while Bei--Navjeevan starts only after a uniformly Gaussian primitive experiment is available. The prior spectral-panel review independently exposes a nearby delta-method construction whose causal interpretation uses post-transport but whose target-pre-span restriction is unused. The missing work is therefore a donor-measurable, minimal-assumption general-r reduction to the full Gaussian-plus-quadratic experiment, followed by regime-free inversion and proof that conservatism costs only the quadratic scale rather than a fixed projection radius.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit donor-only confidence interval with uniform asymptotic coverage over the fixed-r strong-factor class, expected length within a universal constant of sigma sqrt(||uA^+||^2+||A^+v||^2)+sigma^2||A^+||_F, Gaussian-oracle length along every first-order-dominant sequence, and a matching interior local-KL expected-length lower bound.

method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides an adjacent conservative-inversion strategy for the curved null set generated by the bilinear reduced experiment.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the truncated-SVD counterfactual interval be implemented with certified floating-point SVD, cutoff, pseudoinverse, and spectral-gate errors while preserving coverage and adding o(w(P)) expected length uniformly, including repeated singular values and joint-zero loadings?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Backward stability only shows that software solved a nearby matrix problem; it does not ensure that reported endpoints enclose the exact-real interval because cutoff and gate decisions are discontinuous and pseudoinverse errors amplify near a threshold. Repeated singular values complicate vector-level bookkeeping, while joint-zero loadings leave only a second-order statistical width and therefore a much tighter numerical-error budget. Verified-SVD and statistical panel results currently address these two sides separately, leaving the first proof step—deterministic outward propagation through the spectral gate and interval endpoints—unresolved.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-precision algorithm and theorem giving deterministic outward endpoint enclosures and an uncertain-gate fallback, with coverage at least 1-alpha and uniformly o(w(P)) added expected length under an explicit precision schedule, including repeated-spectrum and zero-loading sequences.

writing_exemplar.why: Its last-mile framing motivates treating implementation guarantees as part of valid causal-panel inference rather than as software housekeeping.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Modern matrix-completion theory yields sharp causal-panel guarantees -> practitioners receive floating-point software rather than exact algebra -> spectral boundary decisions can invalidate nominal guarantees -> certified outward computation must preserve coverage and useful interval length

method_exemplars.technique: Use residual-based verified enclosures from computed SVD factors to certify singular-value gates and outward perturbation radii.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The first numerical step is a certified decision about which donor singular values lie above the statistical cutoff.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate multiplicative backward-error bounds for accurate SVD algorithms into deterministic perturbation sets for singular values, subspaces, and pseudoinverses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Multiplicative control preserves relative accuracy of strong donor singular values and bridges floating-point output to an exact nearby experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply explicit first- and second-order truncated-SVD perturbation expansions with remainders controlled by the least retained singular value.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The numerical allowance must propagate through the same second-order TSVD map that determines statistical length at vanishing target loadings.

open_problems.open_problem: Can CAST-style inference for arbitrary bilinear treatment-effect aggregates be made transition-honest when both projected unit and time factor loadings approach zero, with sharp aggregate length rather than projection-width or Bonferroni conservatism?

open_problems.why_unsolved: For a bilinear aggregate, cancellation can make both projected loadings small even when every component entry is regular. CAST sketches the plug-in variance construction but does not prove its bilinear analogue, and its proposed replacement conditions reproduce the nondegeneracy obstruction. Broader synthetic-control intervals do not exploit the exact Gaussian-plus-quadratic factor experiment or establish instance-wise transition length. A resolution must control aggregate cross-covariances and the donor-noise quadratic term before normalization, without reducing the problem to a union of entrywise intervals.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable interval for c1^T M_d c2 with uniform coverage over fixed-r strong-factor panels and deterministic weight sequences, a first-plus-second-order length characterization valid under cancellation, Gaussian-oracle length off the degenerate cone, and a matching local lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents weighted bilinear effects as the estimands demanded by staggered-adoption applications and explicitly leaves the corresponding theorem unfinished in Appendix C.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered-adoption applications require aggregation across units and periods -> these effects are bilinear functionals of a missing counterfactual block -> CAST gives an operational plug-in construction -> cancellation of projected factor loadings requires transition-honest aggregate inference

method_exemplars.technique: Aggregate the leave-one-block-out master expansion before normalization, retaining full covariance and bilinear donor noise rather than summing entrywise bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The aggregate is still a scalar bilinear functional of the four-block SVD experiment, but cancellation makes pre-normalization control essential.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a minimum-distance statistic for the aggregate bilinear map in reduced Gaussian coordinates, retaining the quadratic approximation when its gradient vanishes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Projected unit and time loadings are the primitive coordinates whose contribution becomes first-order degenerate under aggregate cancellation.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its scalable robust optimization and explicit separation of in-sample weighting uncertainty from post-treatment outcome uncertainty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how to expose a bilinear-factor interval as a usable staggered-adoption procedure with uniform post-treatment guarantees.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp transition-honest confidence interval for a missing counterfactual entry when the untreated panel is approximately rank r and the approximation residual belongs to an explicit spectral, max-norm, or factor-idiosyncratic class?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact rank makes the missing entry a donor-block pseudoinverse functional and separates its linear and quadratic stochastic terms. Under approximate rank, the residual creates extrapolation bias not identified by observed donor blocks unless the approximation class controls the missing cell relative to those blocks. Existing approximate-factor central limit theorems address first-order regimes but do not determine how residual bias competes with quadratic transition width when loadings vanish. The first new proof object must therefore be a sharp observable or worst-case residual-bias modulus for a named approximation class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A bias-aware donor-only interval uniformly valid over a specified approximately low-rank class, with expected length equal up to constants to the stochastic transition scale plus a sharp residual-bias modulus, Gaussian-oracle behavior when both residual bias and the quadratic term are negligible, and a matching modulus-based local lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its discussion states the practical robustness question immediately after presenting exact-factor inference, providing a direct bridge from an operational method to the approximation gap.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered-adoption effects are inferred by completing a low-rank untreated panel -> exact factors yield explicit confidence intervals -> real panels only approximately satisfy the factor model -> honest inference must quantify residual extrapolation bias jointly with loading degeneracy

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt nuclear-norm initialization followed by one-step least-squares factor/loading re-estimation and its no-sample-splitting central limit theorem under approximate factor structure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already treats entrywise completion and treatment-effect inference with approximate low rank, providing the first-order component to combine with a transition-honest bias modulus.

method_exemplars.technique: Use observation-probability-adjusted PCA and its joint factor, loading, and imputed-value expansion under approximate factors and general missing patterns.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its imputation theory supplies an analogous separation between common-component estimation and idiosyncratic residual uncertainty.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain the exact-r leave-one-block-out expansion and local genie lower bound as the stochastic core, adding the approximation-class modulus before normalization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution must reduce to the instance-optimal strong-donor experiment when the approximation residual is zero.

open_problems.open_problem: Can counterfactual-entry inference adapt simultaneously to unknown rank and vanishing target loadings, remaining honest over ranks up to a fixed ceiling while recovering known-r transition length whenever the donor spectrum separates?

source_refs.claim: The SVD algorithm and entrywise guarantees take rank r as an input and do not provide rank-adaptive coverage.
source_refs.author: Yuling Yan and Martin J. Wainwright

source_refs.claim: Diversified projections permit low-rank inference without consistent rank estimation and reveal a non-negligible ridge bias from rank overestimation, but do not give transition-optimal missing-entry intervals under staggered donor blocks.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi, Hyukjun Kwon, and Yuan Liao
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Rank uncertainty and loading degeneracy interact: adding or deleting a near-cutoff singular direction changes both the pseudoinverse and the quadratic donor-noise scale, while at joint-zero loadings no dominant linear term can absorb selection error. Choi--Kwon--Liao show that rank overestimation creates a non-negligible ridge-type bias and correct it with diversified projections, but their construction neither exploits the four-block donor geometry nor proves adaptation to known-r instance-wise length. The unresolved proof step is a spectral-ambiguity guard that remains honest at rank boundaries without paying worst-rank width on separated sequences.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A rank-adaptive donor-only interval uniformly honest over a union of fixed-rank strong-factor classes, with an explicit spectral-ambiguity fallback, known-r transition-scale length on separated spectra, and a lower bound characterizing unavoidable length at rank boundaries.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames unreliable rank estimation as an inference problem and isolates the systematic bias caused by overestimating low-rank spaces.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Low-rank causal inference commonly presumes the true rank -> empirical spectra need not reveal that rank reliably -> overestimating rank creates systematic bias rather than variance alone -> counterfactual-entry intervals must adapt to rank while surviving loading degeneracy

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt diversified projections and the explicit correction for Tikhonov-type bias induced by an overestimated low-rank space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly addresses rank misspecification and identifies the bias an honest missing-entry interval must estimate or include.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the rank-r donor SVD expansion and first-plus-second-order variance formula conditionally on a certified spectral gate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the oracle benchmark the adaptive interval must recover whenever rank is spectrally separated.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a minimum-distance statistic over a union of rank-indexed reduced experiments rather than selecting one local approximation before inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Rank ambiguity and loading degeneracy both invalidate a single preselected Wald linearization, while inversion can preserve coverage across neighboring regimes.

literature_map:
Yan and Wainwright (2024, arXiv:2401.13665) are the closest statistical anchor: a four-block SVD estimator, entrywise Gaussian intervals, and instance-wise lower bounds.
Their main approximation imposes a loading-sensitive condition, while Appendix A retains bilinear donor noise for vanishing loadings without constructing a transition-honest interval.
Xia, Yan, and Wainwright (2025, arXiv:2412.09482) develop CAST for staggered adoption and bilinear effects, but Appendix C sketches rather than proves the aggregate theorem and retains projected-loading conditions.
Bei and Navjeevan (2026, arXiv:2602.07377) provide adjacent nonregular-inference machinery through Gaussian minimum-distance inversion near first-order degeneracy.
Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA12030) are a foundational reference for uniform conditional Gaussian inference with nuisance components.
Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi (2021, JASA, arXiv:1710.10251) establish nuclear-norm matrix completion for causal panels but emphasize global estimation rather than transition-sharp entrywise inference.
Bai and Ng (2021, JASA, arXiv:1910.06677) develop tall-wide strong-factor counterfactual imputation and normal theory, preceding the donor-block formulation.
Xiong and Pelger (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1910.08273) treat approximate factors and general missing patterns, but their imputed-value CLT remains first order.
Choi and Yuan (2024, JASA, arXiv:2308.02364) obtain debiased normal inference under MNAR and weaker signals through a split-apply-combine nuclear-norm method.
Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2307.16370) give approximate-low-rank inference; their 2026 JASA paper (arXiv:2311.16440) addresses rank overestimation through diversified projections and ridge-bias correction.
Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen (2023, COLT, arXiv:2109.15154) give causal matrix-completion identification, entrywise rates, and normality under MNAR, but not donor-block transition-optimal length.
Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, JRSSB, arXiv:1912.03290), Cattaneo et al. (2025, ReStat, arXiv:2210.05026), and Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2021, JASA, arXiv:1712.09089) provide staggered synthetic-control and robust uncertainty methods without the first/second-order strong-factor length frontier.
Ben-Michael and Feller (2026, arXiv:2602.21314) identify a practical last-mile problem; verified-SVD work by Terao, Watanabe, and Ozaki (2025, arXiv:2502.09984) and TSVD perturbation work by Vu, Chunikhina, and Raich (2020, arXiv:2009.07542) supply numerical ingredients.
The scan found no complete general-r theorem combining donor-only transition coverage, all-sequence length adaptation, a local-KL length lower bound, and certified finite-precision implementation.
